newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel says has 33 pct market share.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel says has 33 pct market share.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA has a 33 percent share for car passengers in the cross-Channel market as at mid-January, since a November fire disrupted services, the managing director for Le Shuttle tourist services said on Monday.

"Business came back very strongly in December," Bill Dix told a news conference at Eurotunnel's Folkestone terminal. He estimated Eurotunnel would have a 40 percent share of the Channel market by the end of Januray, and is aiming to recover to 50 percent by the end of the year.

Group managing director Georges-Christian Chazot said before the November 18 fire, Eurotunnel held 48 percent of the car passenger market, 48 percent for trucks, 43 percent for coaches and the Eurostar high-speed train had 66 percent of the Paris-London traffic. Airlines had had to reduce capacity last year because of Eurostar competition, he said. "This year will be a year of transition," said French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle. The first half will be dedicated to re-opening the damaged tunnel and restoring full service.
The second half will be one of full recovery, with the company taking back the market share it had before the fire.
No date has been set for a resumption of Le Shuttle freight service, which requires safety approvals. Le Shuttle freight accounts for about a third of turnover.
November's fire started on a lorry on Shuttle wagon.
Some 90 percent of Eurostar trains are now running since the accident, which severely damaged a section of one of the two passenger tunnels.
